extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating data visualizations and infographics in multimedia journalism, covering storytelling, visual design, chart selection, interactivity, data preparation, and tool choice. Aimed at producing accessible, accurate, and engaging data-driven journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of data visualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Data visualization transforms complex information into engaging visuals; it's a crucial skill in multimedia journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use visuals to present data-driven stories in accessible, impactful ways so audiences can grasp key insights quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine storytelling, design, and technical skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective data visualization combines storytelling, design principles, and technical skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists must choose appropriate chart types, apply visual hierarchy, and ensure accessibility. Interactive features like tooltips and filtering enhance user engagement and make data exploration more dynamic and personalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storytelling and visual hierarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: Data storytelling transforms raw data into compelling narratives; visual hierarchy guides viewers' attention to key information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use size, color, and placement to emphasize important elements and organize data in a logical, easy-to-follow structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Color theory enhances data visualization effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ color schemes to convey meaning and evoke emotions; utilize contrasting colors to highlight important data points; consider color-blind friendly palettes to improve accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information design
rubrics_metrics.description: Information design structures complex data for clear communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simplify complex concepts through visual representations and balance aesthetics and functionality in data presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose appropriate chart types
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose appropriate chart types based on data characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select chart types that fit the data and the story you want to tell (e.g., comparisons, trends, composition, relationships).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bar charts
rubrics_metrics.description: Bar charts compare values across categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use vertical bars for fewer categories and horizontal bars for many categories or long labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line charts
rubrics_metrics.description: Line charts display trends over time or continuous data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple lines to compare trends across different variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pie charts
rubrics_metrics.description: Pie charts show composition of a whole (use sparingly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit use due to difficulty in comparing slice sizes; prefer alternatives when precise comparisons are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scatter plots
rubrics_metrics.description: Scatter plots reveal relationships between two variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use scatter plots to show correlation, clustering, or distribution patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heat maps
rubrics_metrics.description: Heat maps visualize data density or intensity across two dimensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good for showing concentration or intensity; choose color scales carefully to avoid misleading interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tree maps
rubrics_metrics.description: Tree maps display hierarchical data as nested rectangles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for showing parts of a whole when there are many categories with subcategories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bubble charts
rubrics_metrics.description: Bubble charts represent three variables (x-axis, y-axis, bubble size).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when you need to encode an additional quantitative variable via bubble size; be cautious about perceptual issues with area encoding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive visualization features
rubrics_metrics.description: Interactive features enhance user exploration and engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include tooltips (additional info on hover), zooming and panning (explore large datasets), filtering (focus on subsets), sorting (rearrange data), animations (illustrate changes over time), linked views (connect multiple charts), drill-down functionality (reveal deeper layers), and custom color selection to highlight specific data points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective visualization techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Design practices that improve clarity and readability of visualizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement consistent design elements across visualizations, utilize white space to prevent visual clutter, incorporate clear labels and legends for easy interpretation, apply gestalt principles to create cohesive visual groupings, and maintain data integrity by avoiding misleading representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure visualizations are accessible to diverse audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use color-blind friendly palettes, provide clear labels and legends, and design interactive elements (like tooltips and filters) so they are usable by keyboard and screen-reader users when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data cleaning and preprocessing
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare data before creating visualizations to ensure accuracy and consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove duplicate entries, handle missing values through imputation or deletion, standardize data formats (dates, currencies), normalize numerical data for fair comparisons, identify and address outliers that may skew visualizations, aggregate data to appropriate levels for meaningful insights, and create calculated fields to derive new metrics from raw data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visualization software and libraries
rubrics_metrics.description: Tools available for creating visualizations, ranging from drag-and-drop to code-based libraries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tableau: user-friendly interface with drag-and-drop functionality and rapid dashboard creation. D3.js: powerful JavaScript library for custom visualizations with fine-grained control and support for highly interactive and animated charts. Other popular tools include Power BI, Google Data Studio, and R (ggplot2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations for tool selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors to weigh when choosing a visualization tool or library.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider learning curve and technical expertise required, integration capabilities with existing data sources, scalability for handling large datasets, and export and sharing options for final visualizations.
